methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

temp.label: TULIP Score

human.outcomeDefinition: Heat illness and impaired access to safe work, food and water
human.estimationMethod: Estimated people actually experiencing the named harm × mean attributable health/function loss-years per person, annual-equivalent at the assessment cut-off. One full function-loss year and one health DALY receive equal index contribution by TULIP choice.
human.attribution: Consolidated current warming consequences; no projected tipping-point collapse, all-cause disaster total or historical-duration multiplier
human.overlapReview: One consolidated consequence estimate within this node boundary; no addition of parent, child or neighbour scores. Human health and service losses are not separate copies. Nature area is assumed allocated once across overlapping habitats.
human.limitations: Order-of-magnitude internal judgment, not a measured global total or validated impact model. Older and regional context is carried to the assessment cut-off by assumption. Local attribution, coverage and conversion remain uncertain. No probability interval is asserted.

assumptions.statement: 500,000,000 actually harmed people is an authored magnitude assumption, not the exposed/dependent population or a source observation.
0.06 attributable loss-years per harmed person includes duration and degree of impairment once. It is an authored consequence-equivalence assumption, not a measured disability weight.

temp.explanation: Internal estimate for Global Temperature: 8.6 out of 10. People: Heat illness and impaired access to safe work, food and water. Nature: Present climate-attributable loss of habitat condition across land and sea. The people component is 8.0 and the nature component is 9.2; each receives half the weight. We use assumptions about how many people are harmed, how much their health or daily life is affected, and how much habitat is damaged. These amounts are not measured worldwide totals. No extra points for permanent loss of rare nature are assigned without enough information about what was lost and how much. Assessed on 28 September 2026 using the available study evidence, which may come from earlier years. This describes estimated current impact, not a ten-year forecast.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for occupational, pollution and water-function losses from mineral extraction and current mine, tailings and freshwater condition deficits; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Actual disturbed footprint and affected communities, excluding hypothetical future mining demand

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

outlook.basis: No future scenario number or historic trend multiplier enters this current estimate.

urban_sprawl_housing.label: TULIP Score

human.outcomeDefinition: Heat, flood and access-related function loss from poorly connected outward growth
human.estimationMethod: Estimated people actually experiencing the named harm × mean attributable health/function loss-years per person, annual-equivalent at the assessment cut-off. One full function-loss year and one health DALY receive equal index contribution by TULIP choice.
human.attribution: Incremental adverse sprawl outcomes; housing provision is not counted as harm
human.overlapReview: One consolidated consequence estimate within this node boundary; no addition of parent, child or neighbour scores. Human health and service losses are not separate copies. Nature area is assumed allocated once across overlapping habitats.
human.limitations: Order-of-magnitude internal judgment, not a measured global total or validated impact model. Older and regional context is carried to the assessment cut-off by assumption. Local attribution, coverage and conversion remain uncertain. No probability interval is asserted.

assumptions.statement: 10,000,000 actually harmed people is an authored magnitude assumption, not the exposed/dependent population or a source observation.
0.025 attributable loss-years per harmed person includes duration and degree of impairment once. It is an authored consequence-equivalence assumption, not a measured disability weight.

ecosystem.outcomeDefinition: Current habitat and hydrologic condition loss on converted land
ecosystem.estimationMethod: Estimated allocated non-overlapping affected area × mean attributable present integrated condition deficit. This integrated proxy is not a measured six-class SEEA profile. No history or recovery-duration multiplier.
ecosystem.attribution: Incremental adverse sprawl outcomes; housing provision is not counted as harm
ecosystem.overlapReview: One consolidated consequence estimate within this node boundary; no addition of parent, child or neighbour scores. Human health and service losses are not separate copies. Nature area is assumed allocated once across overlapping habitats.
ecosystem.limitations: Order-of-magnitude internal judgment, not a measured global total or validated impact model. Older and regional context is carried to the assessment cut-off by assumption. Local attribution, coverage and conversion remain uncertain. No probability interval is asserted.

assumptions.statement: 200,000 km² of actually impaired, allocated habitat is an authored magnitude assumption, not anomaly exposure, a basin count, annual conversion flow or source measurement.
0.5 mean attributable integrated condition deficit is an internal profile-equivalence judgment. It is not inferred from a single species-loss or physical-anomaly percentage.

urban_sprawl_housing.explanation: Internal estimate for Urban Sprawl / Housing: 5.4 out of 10. People: Heat, flood and access-related function loss from poorly connected outward growth. Nature: Current habitat and hydrologic condition loss on converted land. The people component is 3.8 and the nature component is 7.0; each receives half the weight. We use assumptions about how many people are harmed, how much their health or daily life is affected, and how much habitat is damaged. These amounts are not measured worldwide totals. No extra points for permanent loss of rare nature are assigned without enough information about what was lost and how much. Assessed on 28 September 2026 using the available study evidence, which may come from earlier years. This describes estimated current impact, not a ten-year forecast.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for illness and seafood or water-function loss during harmful blooms and current aquatic condition deficits from toxic, shading or oxygen-depleting episodes; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Nonharmful blooms excluded; overlapping toxin, fish-kill and closure reports are consolidated

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

outlook.basis: No future scenario number or historic trend multiplier enters this current estimate.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.

Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.

Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. nitrogen_fertilizer_runoff.explanation: Internal estimate for Nitrogen Fertilizer Runoff: 5.1 out of 10. People: Current usable-water and health or food-function loss attributable to farm nutrient runoff. Nature: Current freshwater and coastal condition deficit from excess nutrient delivery. The people component is 3.6 and the nature component is 6.7; each receives half the weight. We use assumptions about how many people are harmed, how much their health or daily life is affected, and how much habitat is damaged. These amounts are not measured worldwide totals. No extra points for permanent loss of rare nature are assigned without enough information about what was lost and how much. Assessed on 28 September 2026 using the available study evidence, which may come from earlier years. This describes estimated current impact, not a ten-year forecast.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for current usable-water and health or food-function loss attributable to farm nutrient runoff and current freshwater and coastal condition deficit from excess nutrient delivery; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Runoff-specific causal contribution, not fertilizer input tonnage or every downstream algal bloom

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

outlook.basis: No future scenario number or historic trend multiplier enters this current estimate.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for limited current warming-mediated health and function loss allocated to excess tundra methane and present habitat condition deficit associated with adverse excess tundra emissions; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for current water and livelihood function loss from reduced mountain snow storage and present snow-dependent terrestrial and stream condition deficit; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Adverse snow-storage contribution only; no full downstream population as harmed and no future peak-water allocation

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

outlook.basis: No future scenario number or historic trend multiplier enters this current estimate.

methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for current essential-food, medicine and livelihood function loss during harmful port bottlenecks and small present pollution and coastal condition deficit from prolonged congestion; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Essential-function loss, not all delayed cargo value or all supply-chain inconvenience

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

outlook.basis: No future scenario number or historic trend multiplier enters this current estimate.

human.outcomeDefinition: Current housing and recovery-function loss associated with lost coastal insurance access
human.estimationMethod: Estimated people actually experiencing the named harm × mean attributable health/function loss-years per person, annual-equivalent at the assessment cut-off. One full function-loss year and one health DALY receive equal index contribution by TULIP choice.
human.attribution: Nonrenewed policies and insured property values are not loss-years; realized housing deprivation estimated explicitly
human.overlapReview: One consolidated consequence estimate within this node boundary; no addition of parent, child or neighbour scores. Human health and service losses are not separate copies. Nature area is assumed allocated once across overlapping habitats.
human.limitations: Order-of-magnitude internal judgment, not a measured global total or validated impact model. Older and regional context is carried to the assessment cut-off by assumption. Local attribution, coverage and conversion remain uncertain. No probability interval is asserted.

People: Current housing and recovery-function loss associated with lost coastal insurance access. Nature: No independent ecological endpoint within insurance nonrenewal. The people component is 2.9 and the nature component is 1.0; each receives half the weight. methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for current shellfish food and livelihood function loss from impaired growth and survival and present shell-forming community and habitat-function condition deficits; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Current biological outcomes, not seawater chemistry alone or all shell-forming habitat as destroyed

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

outlook.basis: No future scenario number or historic trend multiplier enters this current estimate.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for current chemical-exposure health and livelihood function loss from off-target pesticide drift and present off-target vegetation, insect and water condition deficit; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for current toxic-exposure health and safe-food or water-function loss and present aquatic and terrestrial community condition deficits from harmful accumulated metals; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Dose and chemical form matter; measured presence or tissue concentration is not automatically current health loss

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

outlook.basis: No future scenario number or historic trend multiplier enters this current estimate.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for limited current ecosystem-service function loss from adverse connectivity loss and present habitat connectivity and biological-community condition deficit; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Alternative connectivity view, not an amount to add to fragmentation or species-range scores

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for current safety and essential-access function loss from adverse rock instability and limited present local habitat condition deficit associated with damaging rockfall effects; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Natural rock weathering is not intrinsically harmful; only realized adverse instability contribution

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

outlook.basis: No future scenario number or historic trend multiplier enters this current estimate.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for limited current food and water-function loss associated with adverse pacific wind anomalies and present adverse marine and catchment condition deficit associated with wind changes; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Anomaly sign matters; weakening is not assumed from the node name and natural wind variability is not itself harm

sensitivity.note: Halving/doubling amounts and changing weights are hypothetical stress tests, not confidence bounds, probability distributions or validated model alternatives.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

methodCopy.title: How the TULIP Score works
methodCopy.summary: TULIP Score gives a one-decimal view of estimated current impact on a 1–10 scale. This release uses labelled internal estimates at the 28 September 2026 cut-off. Older source evidence informs some estimates; this is not a measured 2026 global total or a ten-year forecast.
methodCopy.components: People and nature each receive 50% weight in every issue score. People covers attributable health and essential-function loss. Nature covers affected habitat area and its present condition deficit. A zero component needs an explicit scoped absence estimate; missing evidence is never silently treated as zero or given to the other component.
methodCopy.formula: TULIP maps each consequence amount separately against fixed benchmarks, using a logarithmic curve between them, then averages the two scores and rounds once. Benchmarks, health/function equivalence and weights are TULIP choices. They do not change when unrelated topics are added. A documented rare, irreversible ecological loss can add up to 1 point to nature before averaging, at most 0.5 overall, with a ceiling of 10.
methodCopy.missing: Every published issue in this release has an Internal estimate. Its harmed-population, loss-per-person, affected-area and condition assumptions are documented separately from source measurements. These are provisional judgments, not independently calibrated facts. New issues need their own reviewed assessment before publication.
methodCopy.evidence: Historical records and WMO standard normals provide context. Unusualness, exposure, citations and graph connections are not harm amounts. The human estimate represents annual-equivalent health/function loss; nature represents a present condition stock. Their comparison is an explicit TULIP convention. Source years and transfer assumptions remain in the assessment record.
methodCopy.limits: An aggregate score is not the worst local impact or an event probability. Scores for overlapping pathways must not be added. This release has no calibrated confidence interval. Sensitivity tests are hypothetical changes to assumptions, not uncertainty bounds. Response topics receive no danger score. Future scenario outlooks are separate from the current rating.

required: Compatible current global outcome aggregation and counterfactual attribution for current climate-related health and function loss allocated to the bound metal-industry fossil co2 category and current climate-related habitat condition deficit allocated to the bound metal-industry co2 category; independently supported consequence conversion and uncertainty.
evidenceAudit.reuse: Bibliographic and physical context only, except explicitly identified source endpoints. Citations do not validate authored magnitude assumptions.
evidenceAudit.boundaryReview: Actual bound metal-industry category, not a narrower steel-process label and not all particle or mining harm

outlook.basis: No future scenario number or historic trend multiplier enters this current estimate.
